Logistic regression tree by Stochastic-Expectation-Maximization

Source: R/glmtree.R
glmtree.Rd

This function produces a logistic regression tree: a decision tree with logistic regressions at its leaves. The segmentation of the observations is a latent variable: at each iteration a logistic regression is fitted in each segment, a conditional inference tree (partykit::ctree) is fitted to the current segmentation, and each observation is re-assigned to a segment drawn proportionally to the tree probability times the likelihood of its label under the segment's regression. A few good trees are kept along the chain and the best one is chosen according to criterion.

Usage

glmtree(
  x,
  y,
  K = 10,
  iterations = 200,
  test = FALSE,
  validation = FALSE,
  proportions = c(0.3),
  criterion = "bic",
  ctree_controls = partykit::ctree_control(alpha = 0.1, minbucket = 100, maxdepth = 5),
  burn_in = min(50L, iterations%/%4L),
  patience = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

The features to use for prediction (data frame or matrix with numeric, integer and factor columns; characters and logicals are converted to factors). No missing values are allowed.

y

The binary / boolean labels to predict. The larger value (or the second level of a factor) is the positive class.

K

The number of segments to start with (maximum number of segments there'll be in the end).

iterations

The number of iterations to do in the SEM protocole (default: 200).

test

Boolean : True if a test set should be held out, on which the criterion of the best tree is reported in performance (default: FALSE).

validation

Boolean : True if a validation set should be held out, on which the criterion is computed at each iteration to choose the best tree (default: FALSE, the criterion is then computed on the training set).

proportions

The proportions of observations held out: c(test, validation) when both are requested, otherwise a single proportion for whichever is requested. Not used when both are FALSE. Errors when invalid (e.g. a sum greater than one). Default: 0.3.

criterion

The criterion ('gini','aic','bic') used to choose the best tree among the generated ones (default: 'bic'). AIC and BIC are summed over segments (the BIC penalty of a segment uses the logarithm of its size) and are replaced by the log-likelihood when computed on held out data, where no penalty is needed. The Gini index is best used with a validation set.

ctree_controls

The controls to use for partykit::ctree.

burn_in

The number of first iterations that cannot be chosen as the best tree (default: the minimum of 50 and a quarter of iterations).

patience

If not NULL, the chain stops when the criterion did not improve for patience iterations (after the burn-in).

verbose

Whether to print the criterion at each iteration.

Value

An S4 object of class glmtree-class that contains the parameters used to search for the logistic regression tree, the best tree it found, and its performance. Use predict to predict on new data.

Author

Adrien Ehrhardt

Examples

set.seed(1)
data <- generateData(n = 300, scenario = "tree")
fit <- glmtree(
  x = data[, c("x1", "x2", "x3")], y = data$y, K = 5, iterations = 20,
  ctree_controls = partykit::ctree_control(alpha = 0.1, minbucket = 30, maxdepth = 3)
)
fit
#> Error in x$info: $ operator not defined for this S4 class
head(predict(fit, data[, c("x1", "x2", "x3")]))
#> [1] 0.6456856 0.6788915 0.6827978 0.7914840 0.4498238 0.8821124
